text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Following a 24 per cent fall in net profit to A$154.7 million for the half-year to September, building materials giant CSR Ltd managing director Geoff Kells unveiled a radical plan yesterday to approach its main competitors, Boral Ltd and Pioneer Internatonal Ltd, and propose a sharing of the manufacture of key construction products as a way of overcoming the price war that is devastating the industry. Page 1.

Defence Minister Ian McLachlan last night announced British Aerospace had won the A$1 billion contract to provide the RAAF with Hawk jets as the new lead-in fighter for the Australian Defence Forces. British Aerospace was selected ahead of Italy Air Macci and will supply up to 40 jets for the next 25 years. Page 3.

Although figures released yesterday showed a 5.8 per cent increase in the number of new home loans in September, Shadow Treasurer Gareth Evans told an Institute of Chartered Accountants lunch in Melbourne that the Federal Government's mid-term review of the Budget, due within the next two months, was set to downgrade growth and employment forecasts. Page 5.

Announcing a 24 per cent fall in net profit to A$154.7 million for the six months to September, building materials group CSR Ltd yesterday said it would cut its interim dividend by two cents to 12 cents. The company reported record first-half sales of A$.3 billion, in a result boosted by a continued increase in CSR America earnings and a solid contribution from its sugar milling business. Page 17.

Speaking at a business luncheon in Sydney, new Coles Myer Ltd director, Brierley Investments Ltd chief executive Paul Collins, said all aspects of corporate governance within Coles Myer had been "rigorously addressed" and the retailing giant was now ready to get on with "the real business issues". Page 17.

Niugini Mining Ltd chairman Dennis O'Connell, who is also Battle Mountain's chief financial officer and president in charge of finance and corporate development, said yesterday he and new Niugini chief executive Joseph Baylis would meet with all major Niuini shareholders to find out what they want from the company, which is now controlled by Battle Mountain Gold Co.
Page 20.
THE AUSTRALIAN

BHP has raised the stakes at its Glenbrook steel making operation in New Zealand by announcing that a further 200 redundancies, on top of the 400 BHP New Zealand Steel sackings announced in October, will be required if management is to meet tough cost cut needed to rescue the business. Page 19.

In his first major address in Australia in six years, New Zealand-based incoming Coles Myer Ltd board member Paul Collins, the chief executive of major shareholder Brierley Investments Ltd, yesterday urged an end to the feud engulfing Australia's largest retailer, saying it was time to focus on the "real business issues". Page 19.

CSR Ltd managing director Geoff Kells has warned that the company's second half profits this year could be significantly lower than last year after suffering a cut in its net profits to September 30 by a fifth to A$154.7 million, due to falling housing starts and aluminium prices. Because of the poor result, Kells revealed the company will be slicing its dividend payouts. Page 19.

Global food ingredients group Burns Philp & Co Ltd came under fire from disgruntled shareholders at a noisy annual meeting in Sydney yesterday, when shareholders criticised the company for increasing the number of executives earning A$100,000 a year from 5 to 93, while posting a A$62 million loss for the 1995-96 year. Page 21.

Australia's largest steel castings supplier, heavy engineering group Australian National Industries Ltd, unveiled plans yesterday for a major restructure of its Bradken foundry business, a move which involves the closure of two Queensland plants and extenive investment to expand a third in Brisbane, in an effort to cut costs and lift output. Page 21.

Biotechnology group Norvet Ltd has appointed leading immunologist and associate dean of veterinary science at the University of Sydney, Professor Alan Husband, as research and development director, a role which will include supervising the research activiies of the company and driving clinical development of new products. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Confirming the malaise in the building industry, CSR chief executive Geoff Kells has predicted further oppressive trading conditions and tumbling profits well into next year in all its Australian operations after yesterday posting a net profit of only A$14.7 million, a 24 per cent fall in interim earnings. Page 27.

Although Stadium Australia underwriters ANZ Securities, Bain Securities, Macquarie Equities and ABN Amro Hoare Govett were besieged with expressions of interest for the A$10,000 gold passes featured in its A$356 million float, demand has slowed, possibly forcing promoters to accelerate their marketing to overseas clients. Page 27.

Conrad Black's Hollinger Inc has joined its 25 per cent-owned John Fairfax Holdings in calling for a relaxation of cross-media ownership laws, arguing that any change to the media laws should ensure there is no further concentration of media ownership. Page 27.

Angry shareholders at diversified food ingredients group Burns, Philp & Co's annual meeting in Sydney yesterday expressed their dissatisfaction with the group's directors, asking why BBC Hardware had been sold when other assets had underperformed. The shareholders demanded to know when dividends would be reinstated and the board's policy on improving profit returns in the year ahead. Page 29.

The chief executive of Brierley Investments, Coles Myer's newest substantial shareholder, Paul Collins told a Trans-Tasman business circle lunch in Sydney yesterday all aspects of corporate governance had been rigorously addressed within the retailer and said it was time to focus on the real business issues. Page 29.

Following Isi Leibler's purchasing of the Singleton Group's five per cent stake in the Ten Group, three Ten shareholders, Telecasters North Queensland, Robert Whyte and Jack Cowin, will conduct a series of meetings this week to determine the best way of publicly listing the commercial television network. Page 29.
THE AGE

Speculation intensified yesterday that US investment giant Merrill Lynch was set to make a A$94 million bid for Melbourne stockbroker McIntosh Securities after McIntosh asked the Australian Stock Exchange for trading in its shares to be suspended. If a bd is announced, the ASX is expected to examine the frenzy of trading in McIntosh shares last week, which was indicative of insider trading. Page C1.

Amid concerns in business that decisions to cut industry support are being made without considering their implications for growth, Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry president Graeme Samuel announced last night the chamber would convene a conference between business leaders and Government to discuss the direction of industry policy. Page C1.

Pharmaceuticals group Sigma plans to raise up to A$55 million through an issue of shares and unsecured notes to pay down some of its A$100 million in debt from its A$52 million takeover last year of the Queensland firm QDL and to fund further growth. The manufacturer, wholesale distributor and marketer of pharmaceuticals will issue both ordinary and non-voting shares as well as subordinated unsecured notes with a coupon rate of 10.5 per cent a year. Page C1.

The Gandel Retail Trust has lodged far-reaching plans with the City of Stonnington to extend the Chadstone Shopping Centre, in a A$100 million-plus move which would see the Myer department store demolished, two new department store buildings built, more rtail speciality shops and additional car parks constructed. Page C1.

Despite a strong performance by its sugar and US operations and a five per cent revenue increase, CSR yesterday posted an after-tax profit of A$154.7 million for the six months ending 30 September, down from A$204.1 million at the corresponding time last year. CSR warned second-half profits were expected to be considerably lower than for the same period last year. Page C3.

Western Australian iron-ore processing hopeful AUSI has come one step closer to its 1999 production target, following the announcement of a deal with Finnish international engineering giant Kvaerner, which will see Kvaerner inject A$2 million to become a hareholder. AUSI chairman Russel Madigan said project finance was expected to be in place by the middle of next year, with construction of an A$1.5 billion plant near Cape Lambert in the Pilbara to start immediately after. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
